patches.why: the tab's title, a description, and an empty inline icon (a static host has no /favicon.ico: its 404 is the only console error a fresh tab would show)

the simulated engine (dev_mock/fake_engine.js, a desktop test aid) is not shipped; web_page.js takes its place: the isolation service worker, the in-tab socket and the engine. SVK_CONFIG (W3 note §4 item 10): no bridge to ask for ports, W1's data copied beside the page
the title links to the about page: credits, data, licences (a new tab, so the sound keeps playing)
the transport: the page's socket is the in-tab SuperCollider engine (web_page.js → engine.js) instead of a WebSocket to viz/bridge.py; everything else in BridgeTransport is unchanged
the Ground ring block: the desktop carrier ({type:"setn"}, base64 over the WebSocket, for bridge.py to send as /b_setn) becomes engine.js's own upload of the Float32Array into the tab's scsynth
the engine: with no bridge (SVK_CONFIG.noBridge) the desktop page would fall back to NullTransport; in the web build it opens BridgeTransport over the in-tab socket (?engine=off still means silent)

the page boots only when this document will not be reloaded for isolation (web_page.js whenBootable): on a first visit to a header-less host the service worker reloads the page once, and fetches already begun would be aborted (WebKit logs them as errors, and the page's own 'could not start' banner can flash)
the engine chip before the socket opens says what SuperCollider in the tab is doing (loading, waiting for the first click, starting) instead of "bridge: connecting…"
the engine chip's hover names the engine in the tab, not the bridge's ports

sc_patches.why: the Array of 16 SynthDefs inlined; the desktop boot's `.do(_.add)` + `s.sync` follow it in a fork; ~webSynthsReady appended

thisProcess.nowExecutingPath is nil when code reaches sclang through runCode (no file): the folder becomes a literal; it only feeds vizPorts, which the parser reads only when ~svkReplyTo is nil (web_boot.scd sets it)
